evidence: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:38-42: the second OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so as written it covers every WorkflowReminder. But grep shows retryCount is only ever incremented in this file (lines 184, 195), and only for reminders fetched with method SMS (line 50). The column defaults to 0 (migration.sql, schema.prisma:1000), and scheduleEmailReminders.ts and scheduleWhatsappReminders.ts never touch it. So no EMAIL or WHATSAPP row can reach retryCount > 1 today, and nothing is deleted wrongly. Adding `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to that branch is a cheap guard against the column being reused later, not a fix for a live bug.

scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184,195 write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` from a value read earlier (line 58), so two overlapping runs could lose an increment. In practice the cron fires every 15 minutes from one GitHub Actions job (.github/workflows/cron-scheduleSMSReminders.yml:8), so overlapping runs are unlikely. If they did overlap, the bigger problem would be both runs calling twilio.scheduleSMS for the same unscheduled row (duplicate SMS); a lost increment only means one extra retry. Switching to `{ increment: 1 }` is trivial and harmless, so it is worth doing, but the race is overstated.

scheduleSMSReminders.ts:159-177: twilio.scheduleSMS and the prisma update that sets scheduled=true share the try/catch that starts at line 74. If Twilio accepts the message (twilioProvider.ts:104) but the update fails, the catch at 189-197 counts it as a failure, scheduled stays false, and the next run schedules the SMS again. That duplicate path is real but existed before this PR: the old catch only logged, and the row was retried until its date passed. This PR actually caps the duplicates at about two by deleting the row once retryCount > 1. There is also an unflagged problem: the update inside the catch (190-197) can itself throw. If the database is down it will, and that aborts the whole reminder loop.

The scenario is possible: twilio.scheduleSMS succeeds (line 159), the update storing referenceId fails (169-177), the catch increments retryCount (190-197), and a later run deletes the row via the retryCount > 1 branch (38-42). That leaves a Twilio scheduled message with no stored sid, so it cannot be cancelled. But it needs the first database write to fail while the retryCount write succeeds, several times over. And the sid was already lost before this PR, because the old code rescheduled and never saved the first sid. Deleting the row does not create a meaningfully new orphaning risk. The real fix is issue 2's (separate the send from the persistence), not a change for this issue alone.
